Large folio mapcount helper effects and per-VMA accounting rules
Uptodate folio iterator locking, reference, and lifetime guarantees
Filesystem folio read, write begin, and write end callback contracts
Anonymous tracking structure layout and lifetime management
Swap entry translation and shadow cache lookup behavior for evicted entries

findings.text: Registration for a freshly allocated anonymous folio establishes swap backing unless the mapping is droppable, links the folio to its anonymous address space tracking with exclusive status, initializes per-page or whole-folio mapping counts according to folio size class, marks exclusive pages, validates that the covered range lies inside the owning area, and updates anonymous memory accounting including multi-size huge page counters.

Non-exclusive anonymous folios attach to the root of the area anonymous tracking structure while exclusive folios attach to the area local structure, and the tracking pointer combined with an anonymity tag is stored atomically so lockless scanners never observe a torn pointer that could be mistaken for a file mapping.

A new anonymous folio that is not marked exclusive is expected to be held locked by the caller during registration, while exclusive registration relaxes that expectation because no other mapper can observe the folio yet.
Registering an anonymous folio with an address range extending outside the owning virtual area indicates a caller error, as does attempting to register a hugetlb folio through this path.

Anonymous association is carried in folio mapping and index fields, where mapping holds a tagged anonymous tracking pointer and index holds a linear offset derived from the virtual address within the area.
File-backed reverse mapping for a run of pages at page-table entry granularity forwards to a shared file mapping helper with the owning area and table level.

Fault-around installation scans forward from the fault offset for contiguous uptodate folios in the file cache and installs page-table entries for covered pages, returning a no-page fault status when the faulting page itself was installed.

Base-size file cache installation skips poisoned pages and non-empty page-table slots, releases its cache reference on skip, installs only when the slot is empty, and reports success solely when the installed address matches the original fault address.
Fault-around lookup runs under read-side cache protection while page-table installation runs under the page-table lock acquired for the start address and released after the scan completes.

Fault-around bounds are clamped to end of file before cache lookup to avoid races with concurrent truncation, large folio installation across end of file is avoided except for memory-backed files that historically allow it, and successful cache hits reduce the read-ahead miss counter for eligible mappings.
Generic file mapping operations provide a fault handler, a fault-around page installer, and a write-permission preparation handler for use by filesystems without custom mapping behavior.
Generic file mapping setup requires the file cache to support folio reading and records access time before installing generic mapping operations, rejecting files without read support.
Read-only generic file mapping rejects areas that permit shared writable mapping and otherwise behaves like generic file mapping setup.
Constant ENOEXEC reports missing folio read support during generic file mapping setup.
Constant EINVAL reports an attempt to create a read-only mapping over an area that allows shared writable access.
Constant ENOSYS reports generic file mapping entry points in builds where file mapping support is unavailable.
Fault status SIGBUS reports write-permission preparation in builds without file mapping support.

Write-permission preparation holds filesystem freeze protection across timestamp update and folio locking, validates that the folio remains attached to the same file mapping after locking, marks the folio dirty before waiting for stable storage, and releases freeze protection on all paths.

Cached folio read follows a retry loop over lookup, reservation and insertion, and filler invocation, repeating when another thread inserts the same index, when locking is contended, when truncation detaches the folio, when the filler reports truncation, and succeeding when an uptodate folio is found or filled before marking access.
Synchronous cache read helpers wrap a shared lookup and fill routine with mapping default or caller-supplied allocation constraints and return a folio or its member page at the requested index.

Failure to invalidate cached pages after direct writing records a writeback error and emits a rate-limited corruption warning naming the file and writer, since buffered and direct views may have collided.

Direct writing invalidates overlapping cached pages before issuing device transfer, falls back to buffered writing when invalidation finds busy pages, revalidates after completion, advances the file offset by the transferred amount, extends file size for non-block files when past end, and restores unconsumed iterator state unless completion remains queued.

Buffered writing loops over the incoming data iterator in cache-chunk units, throttling dirty pages, interrupting on fatal signals, preparing each folio through filesystem callbacks, copying atomically to avoid fault recursion, finalizing through filesystem callbacks, shrinking the chunk after stalled progress, and faulting the source to distinguish bad addresses from transient pressure.

Generic write dispatch removes file privileges, updates timestamps, directs direct-mode writes to the direct path with fallback to buffered writing when short unless the inode uses direct access storage, and otherwise performs buffered writing.
Generic write iteration serializes checks and data transfer under the inode lock and issues a durability sync when bytes were transferred.

Inode cache invalidation blocks new folio insertion under an invalidate lock, unmaps overlapping page tables, optionally writes back the requested range, discards cached folios across the range while waiting for writeback, and reports accumulated cache errors.

Cache statistics are derived from the file cache index without pinning folios, using entry order to compute page counts clipped to the query range, distinguishing evicted shadow entries from present pages, and reading dirty and writeback tags for resident entries while yielding on scheduling need.

Cache statistics system call validates the file descriptor, copies a byte range, rejects hugetlb files and unexpected flags, enforces write or ownership permission, converts the byte range to page bounds with empty length meaning to end, clears counters, collects statistics, and copies results back to user memory.
Cache statistics permission is granted for writable opens, for owners or capable callers, or when write permission checks succeed.
Legacy page-based cache helpers for unlocking, finishing writeback, waiting for writeback, and marking access forward to the corresponding folio operations on the containing folio.
Cache statistics queries carry a byte offset and length with counters for resident, evicted, recently evicted, dirty, and writeback pages accumulated over the covered page interval.

Evicted entries for memory-backed files require translation to swap entries with validation against poisoned results and may lack a retrievable shadow due to races with reclaim or invalidation, in which case the scan continues without recency accounting.
